subject: general
question: I bought two toy guns for ₹1,200. I sold the first one at a loss of 9% and the second at a gain of 16%. If, on the whole I made neither a loss nor a gain, find the cost price (in ₹) of the first toy gun.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **method of allegation** to find the ratio of **cost prices**.

Loss on 1st gun = −9%, Gain on 2nd gun = +16%, Overall gain/loss = 0%.

Ratio of CP₁ : CP₂ = (16 − 0) : (0 − (−9)) = 16 : 9.

Total units = 16 + 9 = 25 units. Given 25 units = ₹1,200.

1 unit = 1,200 ÷ 25 = ₹48.

Cost price of 1st gun = 16 × 48 = ₹768.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹768.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Total CP = ₹1,200 | Loss₁ = 9% | Gain₂ = 16% | Net Profit = 0.
Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | Loss = CP − SP | Net Profit/Loss = 0 ⇒ Total SP = Total CP.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/07dc25d2bc1ecbf1de5ee6baccd1c61125e8b0275aacf8f010b50e652fb39c46.png] 
⇒ Let the cost price of the **first gun** be x and the **second gun** be (1,200 − x).
⇒ Loss on 1st gun = Gain on 2nd gun (since net result is zero).
⇒ 9% of x = 16% of (1,200 − x)
⇒ 9x = 16 × 1,200 − 16x
⇒ 25x = 19,200
⇒ x = 19,200 ÷ 25 = 768.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹768.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

No Profit No Loss Condition

When an overall transaction results in **no profit and no loss**, the total **selling price** equals the total **cost price**, and the absolute **loss amount** on one part equals the **profit amount** on the other.

Ratio from Percentages

If two items are sold such that profit % on A equals loss % on B for no overall change, the ratio of their cost prices is the **inverse** of the percentage values: CP₁/CP₂ = Profit₂%/Loss₁%.
